sourceIdentity.auditSource: August 14 forensic audit (112 findings: 12 critical, 40 high, 52 medium, 8 lower)
sourceIdentity.note: The full August 14 audit file with all 112 finding IDs was not located in the repository. The 12 critical findings (C01-C12) were investigated and dispositioned. The remaining 100 findings (40 high, 52 medium, 8 lower) require the full audit file to enumerate and assign dispositions.

criticalFindings.title: Secret containment and credential exposure
criticalFindings.rootCause: Secret containment hardened but external credential rotation unconfirmed.
criticalFindings.repair: Hardened .gitignore/.dockerignore for .env.production and variants; rewrote scan-archive-secrets.mjs with deflated ZIP content scanning and broader forbidden file list; strengthened secret-containment-scan.mjs patterns; SEC-01 test passes (3/3).
testsRun: pnpm run release:scan-secrets → PASS (0 violations, 6988 files)
criticalFindings.residualRisk: Credential rotation remains HUMAN_ACTION_REQUIRED. Release remains BLOCKED until rotation is confirmed by a human/external operator.

criticalFindings.title: Terminal persistence scoping/finality behavior
criticalFindings.rootCause: broadcastMatchEnded had a scoping bug: ratingRecord was assigned inside the persistence block but a later `let ratingRecord = null` in an outer scope shadowed it, causing ratingData to always be null.
criticalFindings.repair: Removed the shadowing declaration; retained the persisted record in a properly scoped variable so rating extraction uses the actual persisted record.

criticalFindings.title: Migration 0019 PostgreSQL incompatibility and season fabrication
criticalFindings.rootCause: Migration 0019 used CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION to change parameter signatures and RETURNS TABLE shapes, which PostgreSQL rejects. Additionally, 4 functions still fabricated 'season-1' as a fallback.
criticalFindings.repair: Migration 0019: Changed CREATE OR REPLACE to DROP+CREATE for functions with incompatible signatures. Migration 0022: Patched remaining 4 functions to remove 'season-1' fabrication. Migration 0023: Added composite unique constraint for tournament match IDs.
testsRun: Static SQL analysis confirms no remaining 'season-1' fabrication in function bodies
criticalFindings.residualRisk: BLOCKED: PostgreSQL/Supabase test environment not available. Migration upgrade tests must be run against a real PostgreSQL instance.

criticalFindings.title: Forgeable guest-achievement migration and field name mismatches
criticalFindings.rootCause: 1) Client sends arbitrary sourceIdentity UUID with no server-side verification. 2) achievementProgress array was not validated. 3) Supabase persistor used wrong column names. 4) Non-transactional migration.
criticalFindings.repair: 1) Fixed field name mismatches in supabase-match-result-persistor.mjs (progress→current_value, target→target_value, removed last_match_id). 2) Added achievementProgress validation to validateMigrateGuest. 3) Added BIND_GUEST_IDENTITY protocol message that binds the guest UUID to the connection before authentication. 4) MIGRATE_GUEST now verifies payload.sourceIdentity === conn.boundGuestIdentity server-side. 5) Added BIND_GUEST_IDENTITY and GUEST_IDENTITY_BOUND to KNOWN_TYPES and PRE_AUTH_TYPES.
criticalFindings.residualRisk: The guest UUID is still client-generated. A malicious client could bind any UUID, but they can only migrate achievements FROM that UUID. Since achievements are stored client-side with LOCAL_DEVICE provenance, the impact is limited to importing fabricated achievements. Server-side achievement verification would require a separate guest session tracking system.

criticalFindings.title: Invalid release attestation (CI ordering, manifest hashes workspace not ZIP, PASS hardcoded, recursive CI)
criticalFindings.rootCause: 1) CI pipeline ran release-package before self-audit-generate. 2) ZIP was created before manifest generation, so manifest was not embedded in archive. 3) Manifest hardcoded verdict:'PASS'. 4) verify-extracted.mjs recursed into full CI.
criticalFindings.repair: 1) Reordered CI: self-audit-generate now runs before release-package. 2) Manifest is now generated BEFORE ZIP creation in package-release.mjs, so it is embedded in the archive. 3) Manifest verdict is now computed from self-audit.json status (PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED) instead of hardcoded. 4) Manifest version bumped to 3 with verdictSource field. 5) verify-extracted.mjs replaced full-ci-read-only with focused-tests-read-only to prevent recursion. 6) Manifest verify now rejects hardcoded PASS without verdictSource.
testsRun: node --test test/release-identity.test.mjs test/engine-manifest.test.mjs test/release-truth-closure.test.mjs → 23 pass, 0 fail
criticalFindings.residualRisk: The manifest still hashes workspace files (not the final ZIP bytes themselves). The manifest is now embedded in the ZIP and the ZIP's SHA256 is bound to the certification. True final-byte attestation (hashing extracted ZIP contents) would require a post-extraction manifest verification step, which verify-extracted.mjs now performs.

criticalFindings.title: Duplicate browser application graphs (dynamic imports of app.js from workspaces)
criticalFindings.rootCause: 65+ dynamic import('../app.js') calls in 6 workspace modules created backedges to the entry point. Cache-busting with ?v=hash created distinct ESM graphs for raw vs hashed URLs.
criticalFindings.repair: Created rerender.js event-bus module that decouples workspace modules from app.js. app.js registers its render() function via setRenderer() on boot. All 65 dynamic import('../app.js').then(m => m.render()) calls replaced with rerender() across 6 workspace files: observatory.js (31), branches.js (11), tournament.js (16), ranks.js (4), evidence.js (2), diagnostics.js (1).
testsRun: node --test test/observatory.test.mjs test/observatory-hardening.test.mjs test/observatory-completion.test.mjs → 131 pass, 0 fail
criticalFindings.residualRisk: The rerender bus is a single-function registry. If app.js fails to register, rerender() is a no-op. This is fail-safe (no crash) but means UI won't update on filter changes.

criticalFindings.title: Missing protocol registry entries (tournament/report handlers unreachable)
criticalFindings.rootCause: 11 implemented protocol types missing from KNOWN_TYPES in validation.mjs.
criticalFindings.repair: Added all 11 missing types to KNOWN_TYPES.

criticalFindings.title: Tournament completes after round one (no round advancement)
criticalFindings.rootCause: generateSingleElimBracket only generated first-round matches. recordTournamentResult did not implement round advancement.
criticalFindings.repair: Added advanceSingleElimRound() and advanceSwissRound() functions. recordTournamentResult now auto-advances rounds. Added winner validation and score consistency checks.
criticalFindings.residualRisk: Swiss pairing algorithm is simple (adjacent pairing with rematch avoidance).

criticalFindings.title: Repository deletes existing registrants (delete-then-insert pattern)
criticalFindings.rootCause: TournamentRepository.save() used delete-then-insert for participants and matches.
criticalFindings.repair: Changed to upsert with onConflict for both participants and matches.

criticalFindings.title: Tournament match-ID collisions
criticalFindings.rootCause: Match IDs used pattern TM_R1_M{N} which collided across concurrent tournaments.
criticalFindings.repair: Changed domain to generate tournament-scoped IDs. Added composite unique constraint in migration 0023.

criticalFindings.title: Nontransactional tournament persistence (3 separate DB calls, no rollback)
criticalFindings.rootCause: TournamentRepository.save() made 3 separate Supabase calls with no transaction wrapping. Errors were silently logged.
criticalFindings.repair: 1) Created migration 0024_tournament_atomic_save.sql defining upsert_tournament_atomic RPC function that wraps tournament, participant, and match upserts in a single PostgreSQL transaction with EXCEPTION rollback. 2) Updated SupabaseTournamentRepository.save() to attempt the atomic RPC first, falling back to sequential upserts with error propagation if the RPC is unavailable (backward compatibility). 3) All error paths throw (no silent failures).
criticalFindings.residualRisk: PostgreSQL migration upgrade testing against a real Supabase instance is still BLOCKED. The RPC function is defined but not yet deployed. The sequential fallback provides error propagation but not atomicity until the migration is applied.

criticalFindings.title: Route lifecycle leaks active sessions (no cleanup on navigation)
criticalFindings.rootCause: Router had no route lifecycle management. cleanupPlay() existed but was never called by the router. WebSocket connections, timers, listeners, and engines leaked on navigation.
criticalFindings.repair: Added _previousRoute tracking in app.js render(). When transitioning from a play route to a non-play route, cleanupPlay() is called (wrapped in try/catch for safety). This cleans up: autosave timers, keyboard shortcuts, visibility handlers, sound engine, particle engine, and session references.
criticalFindings.residualRisk: Cleanup is only triggered on play → non-play transitions. Transitions between different play routes (e.g. /play/online to /play/match) rely on play-app.js internal handling. Network session cleanup between play routes is handled by IRX-H25 but is not yet comprehensive.
